scenarios.title: Publish an exact report without losing its source
scenarios.summary: Repair a report publisher that validates inputs and preserves source and unrelated files.
scenarios.objective: Accept exactly SOURCE TARGET, two nonempty flat relative filenames. Otherwise print Usage: publish SOURCE TARGET on standard error and finish with status2. Reject identical names with Choose different files on standard error/status2. Reject a missing SOURCE with Missing source on standard error/status2. Perform checks in this order; on error print no standard output and leave all files unchanged. On success, copy SOURCE bytes exactly into TARGET, replacing an existing target or creating it. An empty source is valid; do not add or remove newlines. Print Published: TARGET followed by a newline on standard output, no standard error, status0. Preserve SOURCE, all other files and no new temporary leftovers.

cases.name: Empty source is still a file

solution:
if test "$#" -ne 2; then printf 'Usage: publish SOURCE TARGET\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
source=$1
target=$2
if test -z "$source" || test -z "$target"; then printf 'Usage: publish SOURCE TARGET\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test "$source" = "$target"; then printf 'Choose different files\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test -f "$source"; then :; else printf 'Missing source\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
staged=$(mktemp report.XXXXXX)
cat < "$source" > "$staged"
if test "$staged" = "$target"; then :; else mv -- "$staged" "$target"; fi
printf 'Published: %s\n' "$target"
scenarios.explanation: Validate the complete request before changing files. Quote names, inspect the actual result and preserve protected data. Temporary staging is a taught strategy; grading accepts any supported solution with the required behavior and complete final file map.
hints: Compare the first failing input set with its expected output, status and files.
Validate every argument before printing a success message or changing any file.
Use quoted filenames and -- for mv/rm; capture mktemp output instead of guessing its name.
scenarios.simplifications: Evaluator18, in-process flat UTF-8 virtual files only. Explicit mktemp TEMPLATE ending in six X characters, single-file mv/rm with optional --. No directories, recursive/force flags, traps, secure randomness, races, locks, permissions, crash durability or Stop/limit rollback. All paths supplied by this lab are flat relative filenames. Final-state grading does not prove an internal staging strategy or real atomic publication.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect expected versus actual standard output, standard error, status and final simulated files for the first failing case. A correct message alone cannot compensate for lost input, an unexpected leftover or changed protected data. Retry after editing.

teaching.prerequisite_note: Builds on exact snapshots, quoted arguments, file tests and conditional shell decisions. The lab supplies arguments and sample files; source, target and staged are variable names your script creates.

concepts.title: Ask before changing a file
concepts.text: Check argument count and empty names before using a redirection: > truncates an existing target immediately. test -f distinguishes a missing source from an existing empty file.

concepts.title: Build a separate candidate
concepts.text: staged=$(mktemp notice.XXXXXX) creates a new temporary virtual file and saves its returned name. The six X characters are a template, not the final name. Always use the returned name in double quotes; never guess it.

concepts.title: Publish and inspect
concepts.text: cat < "$input" > "$staged" copies exact bytes; mv -- "$staged" "$final" moves that file to its final name and replaces an existing ordinary file. -- ends options, so a dash-leading name stays a filename. The source remains. In this model temporary names are deterministic; real security randomness and crash safety are not simulated.

teaching.example:
input='workshop draft'
final='notice.txt'
staged=$(mktemp notice.XXXXXX)
cat < "$input" > "$staged"
mv -- "$staged" "$final"
printf 'Notice: %s\n' "$final"
teaching.inputs: The separate workshop supplies workshop draft and an older notice.txt. Expected output names the final notice; inspect actual files to confirm exact new content and no staging leftover.
teaching.try_change: Change final to board.txt and Run example; notice.txt should keep its previous content while board.txt receives the draft.

scenarios.title: Preview a cleanup before applying it
scenarios.summary: Repair a cleanup tool so previews are harmless and unsafe requests cannot partly remove files.
scenarios.objective: Accept MODE followed by at least one filename; MODE is preview or apply. Otherwise print Usage: cleanup preview-or-apply FILE... on standard error and return status2. Only cache-old, cache spare and -cache are allowed filenames. Validate every requested name before printing reports or changing files. Any other name, including empty or a path, produces Unsafe cleanup request on standard error/status2, no standard output and no file changes. Process allowed requests in their supplied order. For an existing file, preview prints Would remove: FILE without changes; apply removes it and prints Removed: FILE. For a missing file print Absent: FILE in either mode. Each report ends with a newline. Successful requests finish with status0 and no standard error. Repeated requests are allowed: an applied file is absent on the next request. Preserve all unselected files and create no new files.

initial.source:
mode=$1
shift
for file in "$@"; do
 rm -- "$file"
 printf 'Removed: %s\n' "$file"
done

cases.name: Preview all
cases.stdout:
Would remove: cache-old
Would remove: cache spare
Would remove: -cache

cases.name: Apply all
cases.stdout:
Removed: cache-old
Removed: cache spare
Removed: -cache

cases.name: Repeat preview
cases.stdout:
Would remove: cache-old
Would remove: cache-old

solution:
if test "$#" -lt 2; then printf 'Usage: cleanup preview-or-apply FILE...\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
mode=$1
shift
case "$mode" in preview|apply) : ;; *) printf 'Usage: cleanup preview-or-apply FILE...\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
for file in "$@"; do
 case "$file" in cache-old|'cache spare'|-cache) : ;; *) printf 'Unsafe cleanup request\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
done
for file in "$@"; do
 if test -f "$file"; then
  if test "$mode" = preview; then printf 'Would remove: %s\n' "$file"; else rm -- "$file"; printf 'Removed: %s\n' "$file"; fi
 else printf 'Absent: %s\n' "$file"; fi
done

teaching.prerequisite_note: Builds on exact snapshots, quoted arguments, file tests and conditional shell decisions. The lab supplies arguments and sample files; mode and file are variable names your script creates.

concepts.title: A preview is a promise of no changes
concepts.text: The workshop starts with mode=preview. Its first branch prints what would be removed; only the apply branch calls rm. A printed preview is not a preview if the file was already deleted.

concepts.title: Validate the whole request first
concepts.text: The assignment supplies mode and filenames. shift removes the mode from "$@"; for file in "$@" keeps each remaining filename together. Use one pass to reject names outside the stated allowlist, then a second pass to act. A bad final name must not cause a partial cleanup.

concepts.title: Handle absence deliberately
concepts.text: test -f checks whether the named ordinary virtual file exists. An absent cache can be reported without calling rm or emitting an error. rm -- "$file" removes one existing file; the -- protects a name beginning with -. There is no recursive or force removal in this simulator.

teaching.example:
mode=preview
for file in 'demo-cache' '-demo-cache'; do
 if test -f "$file"; then
  if test "$mode" = preview; then
   printf 'Would remove: %s\n' "$file"
  else
   rm -- "$file"
   printf 'Removed: %s\n' "$file"
  fi
 else
  printf 'Absent: %s\n' "$file"
 fi
done
teaching.inputs: The workshop uses demo-cache and -demo-cache, not the assignment allowlist. Expected preview reports both without removing them.
teaching.try_change: Change mode=preview to mode=apply and Run example; inspect files as well as the messages.

scenarios.title: Repair deployment and recovery together
scenarios.summary: Complete a deployment tool that protects the previous report and can restore it without consuming the backup.
scenarios.objective: Accept exactly ACTION CANDIDATE CURRENT BACKUP. ACTION is deploy or restore; otherwise print Usage: rollout deploy-or-restore CANDIDATE CURRENT BACKUP on standard error/status2. After action/count validation, require three nonempty pairwise different filename strings. Otherwise print Choose three different files on standard error/status2. The lab supplies flat relative names; spaces, wildcard characters and leading dashes are literal. For deploy: require CANDIDATE, then require its first line to equal approved exactly, then require CURRENT. On failure print Missing candidate, Candidate not approved or Missing current report respectively on standard error/status2. A final line without a newline still counts as a line. A valid deploy replaces BACKUP with the previous CURRENT bytes and CURRENT with the full CANDIDATE bytes. Preserve CANDIDATE. Print Deployed: CURRENT and newline, status0, no standard error. For restore: require BACKUP or print Missing backup on standard error/status2. Copy its exact bytes to CURRENT, creating or replacing CURRENT. Preserve BACKUP and CANDIDATE; CANDIDATE need not exist. Print Restored: CURRENT and newline, status0, no standard error. Every validation error must leave all files unchanged and print no standard output. Preserve unrelated files and leave no new temporary files. Empty current/backup files are valid. This exercise does not model interruption rollback or crash recovery.

initial.source:
mode=$1
candidate=$2
current=$3
backup=$4
if test "$mode" = restore; then
 mv -- "$backup" "$current"
 printf 'Restored: %s\n' "$current"
else
 cat < "$candidate" > "$current"
 cat < "$current" > "$backup"
 printf 'Deployed: %s\n' "$current"
fi

cases.name: Empty current and approved header without final newline
Restore an empty backup into an absent current
No arguments
cases.stderr: Usage: rollout deploy-or-restore CANDIDATE CURRENT BACKUP

cases.name: Unknown action
cases.stderr: Usage: rollout deploy-or-restore CANDIDATE CURRENT BACKUP

solution:
if test "$#" -ne 4; then printf 'Usage: rollout deploy-or-restore CANDIDATE CURRENT BACKUP\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
mode=$1
candidate=$2
current=$3
backup=$4
case "$mode" in deploy|restore) : ;; *) printf 'Usage: rollout deploy-or-restore CANDIDATE CURRENT BACKUP\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
if test -z "$candidate" || test -z "$current" || test -z "$backup" || test "$candidate" = "$current" || test "$candidate" = "$backup" || test "$current" = "$backup"; then printf 'Choose three different files\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test "$mode" = restore; then
 if test -f "$backup"; then :; else printf 'Missing backup\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
 staged=$(mktemp recovery.XXXXXX)
 cat < "$backup" > "$staged"
 if test "$staged" = "$current"; then :; else mv -- "$staged" "$current"; fi
 printf 'Restored: %s\n' "$current"
else
 if test -f "$candidate"; then :; else printf 'Missing candidate\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
 IFS= read -r header < "$candidate"
 if test "$header" = approved; then :; else printf 'Candidate not approved\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
 if test -f "$current"; then :; else printf 'Missing current report\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
 saved=$(mktemp snapshot.XXXXXX)
 cat < "$current" > "$saved"
 if test "$saved" = "$backup"; then :; else mv -- "$saved" "$backup"; fi
 staged=$(mktemp rollout.XXXXXX)
 cat < "$candidate" > "$staged"
 if test "$staged" = "$current"; then :; else mv -- "$staged" "$current"; fi
 printf 'Deployed: %s\n' "$current"
fi

teaching.prerequisite_note: Builds on exact snapshots, quoted arguments, file tests and conditional shell decisions. The lab supplies arguments and sample files; mode, candidate, current, backup and staged are variable names your script creates.

concepts.title: A recovery copy is the old content
concepts.text: The workshop snapshots workshop-live before replacing it. Copying the live file into a backup after deployment saves the new content, which cannot restore the previous report. Inspect both actual files.

concepts.title: Recovery should not consume its source
concepts.text: mv moves a file; cat < "$backup" > "$staged" copies it. Restoring from a copied staging file leaves the backup available. The independent task also accepts an existing empty backup.

concepts.title: Preflight before mutation
concepts.text: Validate count, action and distinct names before selecting a branch. In deploy, read the first line into a variable and compare it with approved before writing anything. IFS= read -r preserves spaces and backslashes; read may return nonzero on a last line without a newline even though it assigned that line. Check the value, not only read status.

concepts.title: Bounded recovery is not a filesystem guarantee
concepts.text: This capstone grades complete final files and error paths. It does not prove crash-safe atomicity, locks, traps, adversarial-user safety or automatic cleanup on Stop. Those are explicit limits, not hidden successful behaviors.

teaching.example:
staged=$(mktemp workshop.XXXXXX)
cat < 'workshop-live' > "$staged"
mv -- "$staged" 'workshop-backup'
cat < 'workshop-next' > 'workshop-live'
printf 'Workshop deployed\n'
teaching.inputs: The workshop has different filenames and no approved-header rule. Its expected files distinguish the previous live content from both the older backup and next content.
teaching.try_change: Move the backup-copy lines after the live-copy line, then Run example and compare the actual backup. Restore the original order.
